issue.title: Resolve git refs to git revisions [#1331]

repository.name: poetry
repository.description: Python packaging and dependency management made easy

issue.body:
# Pull Request Check List

- [X] Added **tests** for changed code.
- [ ] Updated **documentation** for changed code.

Fixes bug #1331.

body:
@abn I see your point. Even though it might have been undefined or broken behaviour, it makes sense to not break the current flow.

Put differently the following use-cases should be supported:

- git dependency is an editable or development dependency → reference kept and tracked, no "real" locking _(current behaviour)_
- git dependency is just another dependency → resolved to the latest revision and locked there _(what this bug is about)_

For which something as simple as flag could work, e.g. `editable`.
And if the current behaviour is kept the default, then the fix would not even be a breaking change :-) .

Are there other use-cases you were thinking of?

@bibz I think those cases cover the what I had in mind. 

We should probably avoid the the terms 'editable' as that can get confused with editable installs (`pip -e`), which a git dependency might not be. Same applies for 'development' as it is overloaded at the moment. I, personally, like this to be an opt-in behavior if a tag/branch is specified (when `rev` is used it is implicit), and hence an option like 'enforce-revision` or `lock-revision` would be more appropriate.

Should we split this issue into two separate ones?
1. Bug: Lock file does not use revision specified for git dependency if previously a named tag/branch at the same revision was specified.
2. Feature: Support locking revision for git dependencies where named tag/branch are used.

Yes you are right, one bug and one feature.
Would you recommend splitting this issue into two and then closing it? Otherwise I can edit this bug report and make it more constrained, and create a new feature request.
:+1:  I think this can stay as the bug; the PR just needs update I guess. A new feature request  might be appropriate for the feature.

issue.title: Support locking git dependencies to revision when using named references

repository.name: poetry
repository.description: Python packaging and dependency management made easy

issue.body:
- [X] I have searched the [issues](https://github.com/sdispater/poetry/issues) of this repo and believe that this is not a duplicate.
- [X] I have searched the [documentation](https://poetry.eustace.io/docs/) and believe that my question is not covered.

## Feature Request

(Spinned off of #1331.)

The locking mechanism currently pins dependencies to a specific version together with a whitelist of package hashes. This ensures proper reproducibility as every package can be uniquely identified and retrieved.

However this premise does not hold true for git dependencies defined with named references (branches and tags). When locked, their references are not resolved and the named references are copied as-is.

Considering that branches and tags are mutable, this is not a proper locking mechanism for applications. A simple fast-forward (or overwrite) of the reference on the VCS side is enough to change what will be installed by poetry. This is a fragile behaviour when the locking intent is to freeze the dependencies in-place to ensure reproducible behaviour.

_Following the regular locking mechanism, I propose to make git dependencies locked to the revision the reference resolve to. An update of the dependency basically means fetching the remote repository and resolving the named reference again._

This request takes the conservative approach of introducing a new flag to adjust the locking mechanism all the while keeping compatibility with the past behaviour.

### Implementation

There are apparently two use-cases here (see [discussion](https://github.com/sdispater/poetry/issues/1331#issuecomment-526819767) in #1331):

1. A git dependency is a moving target → reference kept and tracked, no "real" locking (current behaviour)
2. A git dependency is just another dependency → resolved to the latest revision and locked there (what this feature request is about)

A feature flag tracking whether a git reference should be resolved would be added in the `package.source` project configuration.

For instance, with the flag named `resolve`:

```
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
mashumaro = {git = "git://github.com/Fatal1ty/mashumaro.git", tag = "v1.7", resolve = true}
```

Yields:

```
[[package]]
category = "main"
description = "Fast serialization framework on top of dataclasses"
name = "mashumaro"
optional = false
python-versions = ">=3.6"
version = "1.7"

[package.dependencies]
msgpack = ">=0.5.6"
pyyaml = ">=3.13"

[package.source]
reference = "f68740f0e344a99e849419da99e96ae5b0bc5ec8"
type = "git"
url = "git://github.com/Fatal1ty/mashumaro.git"
```

### Compatibility

To remain compatible with the current behaviour, the proposed feature could be disabled by default.

I would like to argue that disabling this feature by default makes the locking mechanism more difficult to comprehend. IMHO it is more intuitive to have the locking mechanism be consistent and pinned all dependencies to a unique hash (i.e. version + hashes for package repositories and SHA-1 revisions for git.

### Note

I do not understand the use-case of locking git dependencies to a moving target. But [as pointed out](https://github.com/sdispater/poetry/issues/1331#issuecomment-526819767) by @abn in #1331, this is how the mechanism is used (and relied upon?) today.

body:
This bug has been transformed to a feature request instead (#1348).

@abn: I could not reproduce the bug when locking from a tag to a revision. If you can, feel free to reopen.
